root_cause_CORRECTED.headline: the defect is NOT specific to IInverse and NOT a binding-style problem. On this SW2024 SP5 install the I-prefixed IMathTransform members are not invocable through IDispatch at all, while their non-prefixed siblings work.
root_cause_CORRECTED.why_earlier_rounds_misattributed_it: rounds 1 and 2 wrapped the whole inverse-then-multiply chain in a single try/except. Round-1 candidate C2 (Inverse, dispid 9) actually SUCCEEDED and then died on the IMultiply inside the same try block, so the failure was blamed on the inverse. Round-2 D6a/D6b computed the inverse numerically in Python - never touching IInverse - and still failed 61836, which is what exposed the misattribution.
root_cause_CORRECTED.distinct_error_that_was_informative: round-1 C4 (late-bound 'Inverse') failed with DISP_E_MEMBERNOTFOUND, a DIFFERENT error, proving the late-bound name does not exist while every path genuinely reaching dispid 9/10 got 61836 from inside SolidWorks
root_cause_CORRECTED.project_precedent: identical dual-name class already handled at line 1435 selection_manager(), where the polarity is reversed (ISelectionManager works, SelectionManager fails). The patch follows that established idiom rather than inventing a pattern.
